channel.title: France 24 - International breaking news, top stories and headlines
channel.description: Breaking news and world news from France 24 on Business, Sports, Culture. Video news. News from the US, Europe, Asia Pacific, Africa, Middle East, America

item.title: Melting Himalayas? Nepal disaster exposes growing risk of glacial flooding
item.description: One of the tragic consequences of global warming. Scientists will tell us whether receding glaciers are to blame for last Wednesday’s ice shelf collapse that triggered a catastrophic flood, cascading down more than 3,000 meters from the Chinese border into Nepal.
item.dc:creator: François PICARD

item.title: Glacial flood death toll surpasses 900 in Nepal and Tibet
item.description: Rescuers battled mud and debris Monday as the death toll from devastating glacial floods along the China-Nepal border topped 900, with nearly 4,500 people still missing. Rescue teams continued a desperate search for survivors as entire communities were swept away.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Xi, Putin hold talks ahead of Shanghai Cooperation Organization summit
item.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russia's Vladimir Putin are among the heads of state attending a Shanghai Cooperation Organization summit taking place in Kyrgyzstan. Iran's president Masoud Pezeshkian is also in attendance, where he held bilateral talks with India's Narendra Modi. Marking its 25th anniversary this year, the SCO has strengthened trade ties among its members as the bloc looks to present an alternative to the US-led world order.
item.dc:creator: Yuka ROYER

item.title: Trump threatens to ‘hit Iran hard’ as strikes resume after month-long lull
item.description: President Donald Trump said Monday that the US would hit back against Iranian attacks on US targets in the Middle East, according to a Fox News reporter. The Iranian attacks were themselves a response to US strikes on an island in the Strait of Hormuz, the first flare-up in a month.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Kenya airport staff strike delays thousands of passengers
item.description: In tonight's edition, a workers' strike at Kenya's main airport leaves travelers grounded. Also, Ghanaian cocoa farmers are ramping up their pushback against a new law preventing them from using their land for anything else without permission. And in Tunisia, Sidi Bou Said's been recognized by UNESCO as being important to global heritage.
item.dc:creator: Georja CALVIN-SMITH

item.title: Marine Le Pen's National Rally plans to "sanction" the wearing of the veil with a fine
item.description: The National Rally plans to "penalize the wearing of the Islamic veil" with "a fine" if it comes to power, MP Jean-Philippe Tanguy, Marine Le Pen's lieutenant in the presidential election, stated on Sunday. "We will obviously fight Islamist ideology and we will penalize the wearing of the veil, also in solidarity with all the women around the world who are forced to wear it and who die for this freedom," the MP said. FRANCE 24's Monte Francis reports.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Nepal disaster: fake and AI images flood social media as deaths mount
item.description: As deadly floods hit the Nepal-China border, social media is being flooded with fake and misleading footage. In Truth or Fake, Vedika Bahl goes through viral videos falsely linked to the disaster, including AI-generated content and old recycled footage from India, Chile and Alaska. Some posts have racked up millions of views online, exploiting the tragedy to drive engagement for easy clicks or further perpetuate conspiracy theories.
item.dc:creator: Vedika BAHL

item.title: Macron seals €4.3-bn French frigate deal in Sweden
item.description: President Emmanuel Macron on Monday oversaw the signing of a 4.3-billion-euro ($4.9 billon) deal for Sweden to buy four French frigates as France and Sweden seek to tighten cooperation against a backdrop of growing Russian threats. Sweden is racing to boost its defences after Russia invaded Ukraine in 2022, with the Nordic country becoming a NATO member two years later. FRANCE 24's James Vasina reports.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: 🔴 Former French prime minister Édouard Balladur dies at 97
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Former French PM Édouard Balladur, once defeated by ally Jacques Chirac, dies at 97
item.description: Édouard Balladur, who served as prime minister of France from 1993 to 1995, died on Monday at the age of 97. He led a "cohabitation" government under Socialist president François Mitterrand before waging a bitter battle for the presidency against his friend Jacques Chirac in 1995 – a race he ultimately lost.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Trump vows to hit back 'hard' after first exchange of fire with Iran in weeks
item.description: Donald Trump threatened to hit Iran "hard" after the two foes traded fire for the first time in over a month, while Iran's president warned that more fighting with the US was not in his country's interest. After six months of war, the foes remain at an impasse, with Iran keeping the strategic Strait of Hormuz closed and the US persisting with a naval counter-blockade of Iran. FRANCE 24's Reza Sayah reports from Tehran.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Hundreds feared stuck in hydropower tunnels as flood deaths surpass 950 in Nepal and China
item.description: Rescuers raced Monday to free hundreds of workers believed to be trapped in tunnels at hydropower sites that were buried in mud by catastrophic flooding on the Nepal-China border, as the death toll climbed and increasingly desperate families searched for missing loved ones. FRANCE 24's Eliza Herbert reports.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Raising the Altalena: Netanyahu digs up sunken 1948 arms ship in ‘pre-election stunt’
item.description: A ship carrying arms for a right-wing militia, the Altalena was sunk 78 years ago off the coast of Tel Aviv at the orders of Israel’s founders. The discovery of its wreckage last week has given the country’s right-wing government ammunition to target the left and attempt to redirect the campaign for legislative elections in October.
item.dc:creator: Stéphanie TROUILLARD

item.title: France targets Shein and Temu with new fast fashion levy
item.description: Starting this week, France will charge a penalty on cheaply made clothing sold by ultra-fast fashion retailers, with the fee reaching nearly €20 per item by 2030. Aimed at platforms like Shein, Temu and AliExpress, the levy follows a June law targeting disposable fashion's environmental toll, though rival brands like H&M and Zara are exempt.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Nepal floods 'unprecedented', requires new 'engineering approaches, risk-sensitive urban planning'
item.description: Genie Godula is pleased to welcome Dr. Basanta Raj Adhikari, Director of the Center for Disaster Studies at Tribhuvan University’s Institute of Engineering. He describes the disaster as an illustration of the limits of conventional prevention in the Himalayas. With flood velocities estimated at 170 to 180 kilometres per hour and hazards ranging from ice and snow avalanches to glacial lake outburst floods, he argues that comprehensive monitoring of Nepal’s exceptionally steep and complex mountain terrain is effectively impossible. Yet Adhikari’s analysis is not fatalistic. Instead, he shifts the emphasis from attempting to predict every extreme event toward risk-informed adaptation. Nepal, he argues, should identify high-risk hotspots through satellite observation, supplement these with ground-based monitoring and early-warning systems, and incorporate that knowledge into risk-sensitive land-use planning.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Latest flare-up between US and Iran bring conflict's lull to an end
item.description: Iran's foreign minister has accused Israel's Benjamin Netanyahu of tricking the United States into war with the Islamic Republic. Over six months into the conflict, there appears to be no end in sight. This after the US struck sites in Iran, prompting Tehran to respond. An April ceasefire brought an end to intense fighting, but sporadic attacks have continued over the Strait of Hormuz. Tehran's closure of the waterway during the conflict has pressured global oil markets, and in turn Donald Trump at home.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: 🔴 Lionel Messi retires from Argentina national team after 21 years
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: 'It hurts': Lionel Messi retires from Argentina national team after 21 years
item.description: Lionel Messi said on Monday he is retiring from international football after leading Argentina to a second successive World Cup final in July.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Canberra's zoo treats its residents to personnalised musical therapy
item.description: A music therapist in Australia has been playing for animals at Canberra's zoo for the last five years. It's a relaxing experience for animals and staff alike and the animals all react differently to the music played.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: As Icelanders say no to resuming EU talks, what issues weighed in the election?
item.description: Iceland's voters rejected restarting negotiations to join the European Union in a referendum that pitted concerns about geopolitical stability against keeping national control of Iceland’s prized fisheries. Talks with the EU to join the bloc had begun after the 2008 financial crisis but had been ended by a Eurosceptic government. But why did Icelanders say no? FRANCE 24's Armen Georgian tells us more.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Spain blames Israel, Russia for spreading disinformation during Ceuta crisis
item.description: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez said there were signs Russia and Israel had spread the disinformation over Spain's migration policy that triggered last month's rush of migrants into Ceuta, but no evidence of Moroccan ​involvement. Both Israel and Russia have denied their involvement. Over 72,000 migrants ‌irregularly crossed from Morocco into the tiny Spanish territory between July 30 and 31 ⁠in an unprecedented surge. FRANCE 24's Sarah Morris tells us more.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Nepal deadly floods: FRANCE 24 report – on the ground with survivors
item.description: In Nepal, after the deadly flood, another ordeal begins for the survivors: finding shelter, food, and simply the means to survive. While rescue workers continue searching for possible survivors, those who escaped the disaster are trying to rebuild their lives, despite the threat of another flood. FRANCE 24's special correspondents visited Sinchaur in the Nuwako district – one of the villages hit by the flood on August 26.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: In Northern Cyprus, families wait for news of passengers from sunk ferry
item.description: Seven people have died after a passenger boat capsized in Northern Cyprus. 267 people were on board and 23 are still missing. The boat capsized just a few miles off Kyrenia Port in northern Cyprus - a territory occupied by Turkey but not internationally recognised. The ferry has now completely sunk - and the company that operates it says it is "deeply saddened by the tragic accident". It says a hotline has been set up to provide passengers' relatives with information.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: With no clear contender, "everyone thinks they have a shot"' at succeeding to Macron
item.description: There are eight months left until the next french Presidential election, politicians are ramping up their campaigning, with interviews, meetings and public statements. As it gets closer, more and more candidates are vying for a spot on the starting line. For now, far-right candidate Marine Le Pen is topping the polls - what is unknown is who she will be facing in the second round. FRANCE 24's Marc Perelman tells us more.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24
